searchText: exactly, and now you are a proud member of the eth dev community. Would you be here though if it werent for your initial mining tests? Who knows. Mining is a basic introduction to blockchain technology for many. Having a small pow side chain is not a bad idea <@636289909359116290> There is value in GPU/CPU PoW mining as it creates an incredibly censorship resistant on-ramp, where you can take fiat, buy mundane goods and electricity, and receive ETH. I don't think being a useful thing alone is enough to significantly complicate the protocol though. Luckily, there do exist other chains that support CPU/GPU mining. The missing piece to the puzzle here is the ability to transfer assets from one chain to another in a censorship resistant and trustless/permissionless way. Not even remotely a dev, though. I see people getting a basic intro to blockchain tech now with running a validating node. As Micah says, there are chains where people can mine with a GPU. Cross-chain movement of assets is something I’m quite interested in and hope to be a part of.
